claims.text: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a single-phase microstructure.
The unchanged alloy is relatively brittle and prone to cracking under mechanical load.
The unchanged alloy exhibits a large caloric response.
Tin is an example of a ductile, low-melting metal that is fully miscible with the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 matrix.
Adding approximately 5–10 vol% of the selected metal during processing will induce in-situ formation of a fine second phase.
The resulting second phase will be interconnected and distributed along grain boundaries and within the bulk matrix.
Controlled cooling or heat treatment will cause the added low-melting metal to form the secondary phase.
The ductile second phase will deflect or arrest cracks.
The ductile second phase will improve energy absorption during mechanical loading.
Crack deflection, crack arrest, and increased energy absorption will increase compressive strength.
The minor secondary phase will not disrupt the phase transformation responsible for the caloric effect.
The modified alloy will reach a compressive strength near or above 150 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain its large caloric response with only a minimal reduction relative to the unchanged alloy.
The modified microstructure will mitigate localized stress concentrations under applied fields and mechanical loads.
The unchanged alloy has compressive strength significantly below the proposed 150 MPa target.
The proposed alloy modification remains rare-earth-free.
The selected metal can avoid forming deleterious phases under the proposed processing and operating conditions.

contradictions.description: The additive is described as fully miscible with the matrix, but it is also asserted to precipitate as a distinct, interconnected second phase. No temperature-dependent miscibility gap, reaction, or other phase-separation route is specified to reconcile these statements.
